items.title: Bill Berry and Buster Cooper interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

ctx.x: damn, and we had about an hour to go or something like that. And somebody looked up and coming way across the dance floor at the other end of the ballroom is Count Basie’s band start wandering in. Well that did it. They turned the heat up boy. Man like in one — the next tune it sounded like the world’s greatest band. And it was. But they had, you know that thought, oh, here comes some of Basie’s guys, we’ll have to show ‘em how to do it.

[inaudible]. You know I’ve seen us play, you know, jazz festivals with the band and everything. And it’s like Duke’s band was always the last one to go on. You know, nine times out of ten. It’s a lot of hanging around, so you get kind of sluggish you know. And Paul gets more than anybody, Paul Gonsalves. So what happened was, and all the musicians were around and everything, and in the opening the band is kind of tired out now, you know. And the band would sound terrible to me, you know. Okay now the next night…
